notes: Each case starts from the repo state in `setup`, prepared by the runner before the agent starts. Prompts answer the skill's questions up front and give the go-ahead for the plan, so a run needs no human; the go-ahead never covers an item the plan marks optional. Run with DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 so eval installs stay out of the skills.sh counts, tell the agent to count the machine as having no companion skills, and forbid every write to a remote: the fixtures' remotes point at repositories that are not ours.

evals.setup: An empty git repo with one remote, origin = https://github.com/acme/ledger.git, and no commits.
evals.prompt: Set up this repo for a new Python service called ledger: an HTTP API that records card payments, deployed and never installed as a package. I work on it with two colleagues and we track work in GitHub issues. It reads STRIPE_API_KEY and DATABASE_URL; both live in 1Password (vault "ledger") and in the GitHub environment prod, and the payments team owns them. License: MIT. Release process: we tag vX.Y.Z on main, GitHub Actions builds the image and deploys it to Fly.io, and we never deploy on a Friday. Amounts are always integer cents, never floats. You have the go-ahead for the plan you show.
evals.expected_output: A uv service scaffold with the cross-cutting files, a CI workflow with pinned actions, a short AGENTS.md with the marker, the fifteen precepts, the workflow, the skills lines and a map, CLAUDE.md and the Gemini settings, docs/ with the index, Matt's GitHub tracker files, triage labels and secrets.md, a user-only release skill built only from the given facts, the companion skills in two real copies, and a hand-over with the verify results.
assertions: uv init ran with --app --no-package and --author-from none; pyproject.toml and uv.lock exist
AGENTS.md is under 100 lines, starts with the bushido-setup marker, and carries the Precepts block from references/precepts.md word for word
AGENTS.md holds the integer-cents rule and no overview, directory tree or stack summary
CLAUDE.md holds exactly @AGENTS.md; .gemini/settings.json lists AGENTS.md in context.fileName
docs/README.md lists every entry of docs/; docs/agents/ holds issue-tracker.md from the GitHub template, domain.md and triage-labels.md
docs/secrets.md has one row each for STRIPE_API_KEY and DATABASE_URL with no value; .env.example lists both names with empty values; .claude/settings.json denies reading .env

A release process skill sits in .agents/skills and .claude/skills with disable-model-invocation: true and agents/openai.yaml allow_implicit_invocation: false, holds only the given facts (tag vX.Y.Z, Actions to Fly.io, no Friday deploys), and AGENTS.md lists it

The companion skills sit as real files in .agents/skills and .claude/skills, identical except code-review, which is only in .agents/skills; to-spec, to-tickets and triage are included; skills-lock.json lists them all
ci.yml has a code job with the uv commands and a docs job with lychee and the agent-files check; every action is pinned to a full commit SHA
LICENSE is MIT; dependabot.yml has the github-actions and uv entries, and the hand-over says to check Dependabot's first run
No ARCHITECTURE.md, no GLOSSARY.md or ADR without content, and CHANGELOG.md with an Unreleased section, since tagged releases are shipped versions
Lint, format check, type check and tests ran and passed; the hand-over reports them and the always-loaded line count
ruff, mypy and pytest are configured to skip .agents and .claude
The hand-over lists the files the release process relies on and the repo lacks (the deploy workflow, a Dockerfile, fly.toml) without writing them

evals.setup: An empty git repo with origin = https://github.com/me/dashboard.git and no commits.
evals.prompt: Set up a new TypeScript web app with React: an internal dashboard. Only I work on it and I don't use an issue tracker. No secrets. No license, it's private. Nothing special an agent needs to know yet. You have the go-ahead for the plan you show.
evals.expected_output: A Vite react-ts scaffold with its own linter kept, the cross-cutting files, CI, and the agent files without any file that would be empty: no secrets doc, no license, no process skill, no glossary.
assertions: npm create vite ran with --template react-ts (the skill's default for a single package); the Oxlint setup it installed is kept and Biome was added as the formatter alone
No LICENSE file; no docs/secrets.md and no .env.example; no process skill; no GLOSSARY.md, docs/adr/ or CHANGELOG.md
to-spec, to-tickets and triage are not installed; docs/agents/ holds no issue-tracker.md and no triage-labels.md, and AGENTS.md has no Issue tracker section
AGENTS.md is under 100 lines, carries the precepts word for word, and its Commands section holds only commands an agent would not guess
The CI code job runs the scaffold's lint, type check and tests; the docs job runs lychee and the agent-files check
The project's lint and tests ran and passed

evals.setup: A Node library repo with one commit: package.json (name "slugkit", type module, scripts test = "vitest run" and codegen = "node scripts/codegen.mjs", devDependencies vitest and typescript), a package-lock.json, src/index.ts, src/index.test.ts, src/generated/tables.ts, scripts/codegen.mjs, README.md, LICENSE (MIT), and a hand-written CLAUDE.md of about 30 lines with: a two-paragraph project overview; 'Run npm test before every commit'; 'Never edit src/generated/ by hand, run npm run codegen'; 'Use 2-space indentation'; 'Keep functions under 20 lines'; 'Prefer small commits'. Also .cursor/rules/style.mdc repeating 'Keep functions under 20 lines'.
evals.prompt: Set up this existing repo for coding agents. Answers: it's a Node library; I maintain it and outside contributors send pull requests; no secrets; keep the existing license; I don't use an issue tracker. You have the go-ahead for the plan you show, including the merge of the existing agent files.
evals.expected_output: Nothing the user wrote is lost: CLAUDE.md is merged into AGENTS.md and becomes @AGENTS.md, the generated-code rule moves into a src/generated pair listed in the map, duplicates and the contradiction with precept 7 are reported, and package.json, the lockfile, the README and the license are untouched.
assertions: package.json, package-lock.json, README.md and LICENSE are byte-identical to the fixture; npm init never ran
No formatter or fixer ran in write mode on the existing sources; a missing formatter or linter appears in the plan only as an optional item
CLAUDE.md holds exactly @AGENTS.md
Every rule of the old CLAUDE.md is in AGENTS.md, in src/generated/AGENTS.md, or reported as a duplicate of a line kept elsewhere
The plan reported 'Keep functions under 20 lines' as contradicting precept 7 and showed both versions
The overview paragraphs were not copied into AGENTS.md; the plan says where they went (README or dropped as an overview) and the user's go-ahead covered it
src/generated/AGENTS.md and its CLAUDE.md exist, and the AGENTS.md map lists src/generated/AGENTS.md
.cursor/rules/style.mdc was merged and removed only as part of the confirmed plan
CONTRIBUTING.md exists because outside contributors send pull requests
The project's tests ran and passed

evals.setup: The output of python-service-new, committed, then changed in a second commit: an 'Overview' section of 30 lines added to AGENTS.md (now 120 lines); tests/AGENTS.md added with its CLAUDE.md but not listed in the map; .claude/skills/tdd/SKILL.md edited so it differs from .agents/skills/tdd/SKILL.md; docs/runbook.md added and not listed in docs/README.md; SENTRY_DSN added to .env.example and not to docs/secrets.md.
evals.prompt: Audit this repo. Show me the report and the fixes you propose; I have not confirmed any fix yet.
evals.expected_output: A report of at most 30 lines naming each of the five drifts with its file and a one-line fix, the rest summarised as a count, and a proposed plan; no file changed.
assertions: The report names AGENTS.md as over 100 lines and the Overview section as content to remove
The report names tests/AGENTS.md as missing from the map
The report names the tdd skill copies as different
The report names docs/runbook.md as missing from docs/README.md
The report names SENTRY_DSN as missing from docs/secrets.md
git status shows no change after the run

evals.setup: A Maven repo with one commit: pom.xml, mvnw, .mvn/, src/main/java/com/acme/App.java, src/test/java/com/acme/AppTest.java, a .gitignore with 'target/', and origin = https://github.com/acme/billing-java.git.
evals.prompt: Set up this repo for coding agents. It's a Java service; build and test with ./mvnw verify. Our team of four tracks work in GitHub issues. No secrets in this repo. License: Apache-2.0. You have the go-ahead for the plan you show.

assertions: No generator ran; pom.xml, mvnw and the sources are unchanged
The existing .gitignore kept its lines and gained only missing ones from the Maven or Java template, under a # bushido-setup comment
ci.yml's code job runs ./mvnw verify; the docs job runs lychee and the agent-files check
LICENSE is Apache-2.0
AGENTS.md carries the precepts word for word and is under 100 lines

evals.setup: An empty git repo with origin = https://github.com/acme/tidy.git and no commits.
evals.prompt: Set up a new Go command-line tool called tidy that cleans up old git branches. Only me, no issue tracker, no secrets, MIT license. Release process: I push a tag vX.Y.Z, goreleaser builds the binaries in GitHub Actions, and then I update the Homebrew formula in acme/homebrew-tap by hand. You have the go-ahead for the plan you show.
evals.expected_output: A go.mod with main.go at the root, golangci-lint config version 2, the cross-cutting files and CI, and a user-only release skill holding exactly the three steps the user gave.
assertions: go mod init ran with github.com/acme/tidy; main.go sits at the root; no pkg/ folder
.golangci.yml has version: "2"
The release skill holds exactly the three given steps (tag push, goreleaser in Actions, Homebrew formula by hand) and nothing invented, such as changelog generation or signing
The release skill has disable-model-invocation: true and agents/openai.yaml allow_implicit_invocation: false, in both skill folders, and AGENTS.md lists it
gofmt, go vet and go test ran and passed

evals.expected_output: The marker sends the run to the audit; every item is fine and no file changes.
assertions: The run recognised the marker and ran the audit instead of the setup
The report says every item is fine, or names only items the run can show are real
git status shows no change after the run

ab_test.question: Do precepts written with references/writing.md get followed better, or cost fewer tokens, than the same precepts in loose prose?

variants.A: AGENTS.md as the skill wrote it.
variants.B: AGENTS.md with the Precepts block replaced by one paragraph of loose prose saying the same fifteen things.

ab_test.task: In a fresh session, ask: 'Add an endpoint that refunds a payment by id, and fix the bug that lets a refund exceed the original amount.' Run it three times per variant.
measures: Behaviour change shipped with tests in the same commit, and the bug fix started from a failing test
Commits are Conventional Commits, with the refactor committed apart from the behaviour change
Amounts stay integer cents; configuration is read through the existing config module
Docs or docs/agents updated when the behaviour they describe changed
Tokens of the root AGENTS.md (count with the agent's own tokenizer when available)
